body.x: CNAI (CEO WonSeop Lee) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

CNAI was founded in 2019 with the goal of becoming a global synthetic data leader. Ever since, the Korean company has long accumulated know-how and numerous patents in the field of AI synthetic data. Their synthetic data for AI learning based on the actual data can significantly reduce the cost and time for data collection, and the company can generate edge case data that is difficult to acquire in the real world.

As such, CNAI's AI synthetic data technology specialized in images and videos has been introduced in diverse industries such as healthcare, finance, retail, manufacturing, and defense, facilitating success of projects and securing market competitiveness.

The startup presented their core synthetic data related technology Data Acceleration at CES 2023. Data Acceleration is a technique in which an AI algorithm analyzes an existing dataset to determine the area that lacks quantity, and automatically generates data for supplementation to improve the quantity and quality of data. The enhanced dataset can be used to reinforce AI performance. This technology is being used for disease diagnostics solutions and defective product inspection solutions developed by CNAI.

Selected by MIT Technology Review as one of the “Top 10 Breakthrough Technologies 2022,” synthetic data has been noted as an innovation that dramatically reduces the time and cost required to collect data needed to improve AI performance. In line with this, CNAI has been chosen by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups as “Best Public-Private Open Innovation Business Company” and won “2022 AI Startup 100” and the “Best 2022 Fourth Industrial Revolution Award” in recognition of their technology and growth potential in this innovation field.

In addition, supported by different customers including banks, hospitals, and public institutions in South Korea, CNAI is expanding its client base while providing high-quality output and winning additional projects. It also aims to discover potential overseas customers in this CES.

“We are confident that our expertise in developing synthetic data and AI engines has an extraordinary potential in the field of vision AI,” said a CNAI representative. They added, “With these core technologies, we are pursuing development of related solutions such as AI CCTV, Smart City, and AI Medical.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
